title: Ar-Rahman, the Most Merciful
hookLine: the Most Merciful, mercy vast enough for all creation, even the people who made this week hard
tomorrow: mercy for everything. but does it ever find just one person?

lines: THE LIST FROM A ROUGH WEEK.
cards: A rough week leaves a list: the teacher who snapped, the driver who cut you off, the group chat that went cold for no reason. Box one on yesterday's grid gets a name big enough to cover every person on that list, and you.
Ar-Rahman. In Pickthall's English, the Beneficent. It's the first name in Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim, the words that open surah after surah.

teach.b: The name comes from the root of mercy, r-h-m. Here's how big it is, in a hadith Bukhari and Muslim record, in paraphrase. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, said: Allah made mercy in a hundred parts.
He kept ninety-nine with Himself and sent one part down to earth.
From that one part, creatures show mercy to each other, so that a mare lifts her hoof away from her foal, afraid of hurting it.
That's the thing to tell a friend tonight: every kind act you've ever seen, a nurse at three in the morning, a stranger holding a door, a horse stepping carefully, comes from one part in a hundred.
Ar-Rahman is the name for the whole.
In Surah al-A'raf, Pickthall has: and My mercy embraceth all things. All things includes the teacher who snapped. That doesn't make what he did fine; the Qur'an speaks of justice too.
It means nobody on this week's list was standing outside the reach of that mercy. Neither were you. That can change how a hard week ends: not with a verdict, but with a wider view.

how: Muslims say Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim before reciting the Qur'an and before many everyday acts, naming Allah's mercy first.

o: the Most Merciful, mercy that reaches everyone
the Patient One, who waits before He acts
the King who rules the heavens and the earth

games.q: mercy for all — tap the pairs.
p: lifts her hoof from her foal

s: in the hadith, all the mercy among creatures comes from one part of a hundred
Allah kept ninety-nine parts and sent one down; even the mare lifts her hoof from her foal.
Ar-Rahman is mercy only for the people who deserve it
My mercy embraceth all things: the name is mercy vast enough for all creation.
Pickthall's English calls Ar-Rahman the Beneficent
his translation says the Beneficent; the root is mercy, r-h-m.

games.q: a coworker blamed you for her mistake in front of everyone, then acted normal the next day. what does Ar-Rahman's mercy say about her?
o: she's outside mercy until she apologizes.
mercy reaches her too; that doesn't make what she did okay.
mercy means pretending it never happened.
games.why: My mercy embraceth all things: the person who wronged you is inside its reach. that isn't the same as calling the wrong right.

practice: Look around for one thing that's here because someone was kind: a gift, a meal, a chair somebody carried in. Rest your eyes on it for the sit. Let it count as a trace of that one part sent down.

carryVoice: For today: mercy for all, the ones who were hard to like this week included. Box one, filled.
